> **What this case shows** — **ENMO** truncates the vector-magnitude-minus-1g to zero, so any dip
> *below* 1 g — deceleration, partial free-fall, or a persistent calibration offset — is thrown away.
> **ENMOa** keeps it by taking the absolute value instead. The ecosystem had ENMO and MAD, both
> GGIR-certified; this case adds the third, **`computeENMOa`**. On a real free-living recording it
> reproduces `GGIR::g.applymetrics` ENMOa to **machine precision** (max |diff| ~**2e-14 g**), and it
> shows the consequence: ENMOa exceeds ENMO by **~63 mg** — the sub-1 g movement ENMO discards.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — `computeENMOa(accel, sampling_rate, epoch_sec)` → per-epoch mean |r − 1|.
**Way of thinking** — ENMO's truncation is a deliberate choice: it assumes sub-1 g excursions are
noise. ENMOa assumes they are movement. On perfectly calibrated data they nearly agree; where they
diverge, you are seeing either real below-1g dynamics or a calibration offset — either way, worth
knowing.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioWearable::computeENMOa()` with `computeENMO()` and `computeMAD()` — the
three GGIR-certified accelerometer movement metrics.
:::

## Proposition

On real PAMAP2 hand-accelerometer data (749 epochs of 5 s at 100 Hz), `computeENMOa` reproduces
`GGIR::g.applymetrics` ENMOa to machine precision (max |diff| ~2e-14 g, r = 1.0); ENMOa ≥ ENMO at every
epoch and exceeds it by ~63 mg on average (mean 224 vs 162 mg).

## Question & goal

**The question is a gap and its fidelity: the ecosystem had GGIR-certified ENMO and MAD but not ENMOa —
can we author the always-positive companion and reproduce GGIR exactly, and quantify how much sub-1 g
movement ENMO discards?** The goal is to introduce `computeENMOa`, certify it against GGIR, and read the
ENMO/ENMOa gap.

## Challenge & approach

ENMOa per epoch is mean(|r − 1|), where r = √(x²+y²+z²); ENMO is mean(max(r − 1, 0)). They differ only
where r < 1 g. We compute ENMOa per non-overlapping 5 s epoch, check it against
`GGIR::g.applymetrics(..., do.enmoa)` on the identical signal, and contrast it with ENMO.

```
PAMAP2 hand accel (x,y,z @ 100 Hz) → r = √(x²+y²+z²) → per 5 s epoch: ENMOa = mean(|r − 1|)
                    vs GGIR::g.applymetrics ENMOa (same signal) → machine precision (2e-14 g, r = 1.0)
                    ENMOa (224 mg) ≥ ENMO (162 mg) everywhere; gap 63 mg = the sub-1 g movement
```

## Data

**PAMAP2 Physical Activity Monitoring dataset (UCI/PhysioNet)**: subject **101**, hand-worn IMU
accelerometer (x, y, z in g at 100 Hz), ~62 minutes free-living — the same git-tracked signal the
[ENMO](../adl-freeliving-pamap2/index.qmd) and [MAD](../mad-freeliving-pamap2/index.qmd) cases use.
Details in [`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: ENMOa (red) and ENMO (blue) per epoch across the recording — ENMOa sits at or above ENMO everywhere, and the band between them is the sub-1 g movement ENMO truncates (means 224 vs 162 mg). Right: computeENMOa versus GGIR g.applymetrics ENMOa, one point per epoch, all on the identity line — machine precision (max |diff| ~2e-14 g, r = 1.0).](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* the left panel is what ENMOa adds over ENMO (the below-1g band); the right panel is
the certification — the newly-authored op lies exactly on the field-standard GGIR.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| op vs `GGIR::g.applymetrics` ENMOa (max \|diff\|) | **2e-14 g** (bit-exact) |
| correlation across epochs | **1.000** |
| epochs certified | **749** |
| **mean ENMOa** | **224 mg** |
| ENMOa ≥ ENMO at every epoch | **yes** |
| mean ENMOa − mean ENMO | **63 mg** (sub-1 g movement) |

The newly-authored op matches GGIR at every epoch, and the ENMO/ENMOa gap quantifies the below-1g
movement. Values trace to [`artifacts/enmoa_summary.csv`](artifacts/enmoa_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`computeENMOa` completes the accel movement triad — ENMO, MAD and now ENMOa, each GGIR-certified — and
it is exact: bit-for-bit against GGIR across a full free-living recording. The transferable takeaway:
**ENMO's truncation is an assumption, not a law. Report ENMOa alongside ENMO when calibration is
uncertain — the gap between them is exactly the sub-1 g movement ENMO chooses to ignore.**

## Open questions

- With ENMO, ENMOa and MAD all GGIR-certified, the natural next step is auto-calibration: an
  ENMOa-vs-ENMO gap can flag a calibration offset on uncalibrated data, turning the pair into a
  data-quality signal. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| ENMO-abs (retains sub-1g) | `computeENMOa()` | PhysioWearable |
| Euclidean norm minus one | `computeENMO()` | PhysioWearable |
| Mean amplitude deviation | `computeMAD()` | PhysioWearable |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **epoch_sec** — aggregation window (here 5 s, the GGIR default).
- **sampling_rate** — required when `epoch_sec` is set (here 100 Hz).
- **unit** — `"g"` (default) or `"mg"`.
- **when to prefer ENMOa** — uncalibrated data, or when sub-1 g dynamics matter; otherwise ENMO's
  truncation suppresses gravity-residual noise.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioWearable)

enmoa <- computeENMOa(accel, sampling_rate = 100, epoch_sec = 5)   # per-epoch |r-1| (g)
# reproduces GGIR::g.applymetrics ENMOa to machine precision; ENMOa >= computeENMO().
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/enmoa_summary.csv`](artifacts/enmoa_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks the
bit-exact GGIR agreement (max |diff|, correlation), the epoch count, the mean ENMOa, the ENMOa ≥ ENMO
relationship and the sub-1g gap, and the honestly-noted scope (newly-authored op; machine-precision;
ENMOa a physical quantity completing the ENMO+MAD+ENMOa triad).
